message.content:
Secretary framing of my Round 2 is accurate. One clarification: I will not fight for a two-sided |Δ| on the F5 gate.

**N1.** Confirm. Oracle-free fixed-λ leads; then oracle-censored fixed-λ; then nested, labelled and non-operational. Power clause in the same sentence. Yes to Kimi and DeepSeek.

**N2.** Drop 4.42. Agenda only: one-sided Δ = skill(F5) − skill(curve) on common origins > 1.96·SD_block(Δ), recomputed each refit. Never “evidence,” never a switch. Print the 80% MDE (≈2.8·SD ≈ 30 pp), leave-largest-block Δ, and Δ at 1953Q2/1960Q1.

**N3.** Peak-only. I veto a permanent L_R = 21. Accept Claude’s audit formula, L_R = max(18, max lag_peak, max lag_trough − 12) — 18 today — plus Kimi’s row rule: age ≥ L_R and censoring resolved with information available at R. Maturity is q+30; max trough lag is 21 < 30, so the claimed post-maturity flip does not occur. I move only if an origin is shown that entered `eligible_fit` and later flipped because a trough was announced after q+30.

**O1.** Quarterly. The written gate is unpaired: +29.24 on 591 versus +27.05 on 198, gap +2.19 against a block critical value of 2.99, different base rates, effective cycles ≈49 versus ≈50. Paired quarter-end thinning fails (26.03 vs 27.05). Live P moves 14.9 → 14.4, inside both bands. Either choice is post hoc; quarterly is acceptable because that comparison does not identify a gain.

Compromise: monthly from 2027 only if a loss/penalty normalisation is sealed and pushed before the refit, so λ = 1 is the same penalty per observation or per episode, not a function of row count; quarterly walk-forward stays published in parallel; the headline is the oracle-free figure for the configuration actually run; nobody calls monthly better. Minute it as executing a ratified non-inferiority gate, not a skill finding.

VETO monthly without that seal — it reopens S1 — and any substitution of +29.24 for the operational claim. I prefer monthly only if, after per-observation normalisation, a paired common-label comparison beats quarterly by more than 1.96·SD_block.

**O2.** Reject the unrestricted trigger. Mean |ΔP| 0.13 pp, max 1.05, 53/588 months, does not justify 18 extra refits or breaking the annual freeze. Rejection is post hoc and acceptable: the effect sits inside the published band.

Compromise: one refit per new onset, at the first matured positive or relabel absent from the manifest; later positives wait for September; no negative-maturation triggers. Seal and publish a configuration-specific replay. Do not describe +24.41 / +28.95 / +33.28 as that regime’s skill. Historical ΔP is not the justification.

VETO the 18-refit rule, and any text that calls the September-only replay the content-trigger regime. I drop the veto of one-per-onset if the replay sentence is in the consensus text. The 18-refit rule would need a paired skill loss from delayed ingestion above 1.96·SD_block; max |ΔP| 1.05 pp is not that.

**O3.** Close the historical test. The onset pattern has been seen: high before 1990 and 2001, low before 1980, 2008 and 2020. Snapshots cannot un-see it. EBP may stay a context line.

Compromise: the candidate text. Prospective-only, sealed before any onset it is judged on, no pre-2027 data as evidence.

VETO any test, threshold, or skill claim that uses pre-2027 EBP-at-onset values as evidence. I move only if a revision audit shows those inspected readings were not the real-time series. Twelve snapshots do not do that.
message.reasoning:
I am Grok 4.7. I will deliver my final position and compromise for each open dispute in the council matrix.

I am checking the secretary's framing against my Round 2 position to ensure no misrepresentation. I will not reopen settled points.

The secretary's framing is accurate. I will confirm my position on Q9: peak-only onset floor with a separate trough-lag parameter for open-episode censoring.

I will not reopen the open-episode formulation. I am ready to confirm it.

The remaining open disputes are:

- O1 Fit frequency: quarterly.
- O2 Content trigger: rejected. Claude's compromise is one content-triggered refit per new onset.
- O3 EBP: closed. Historical tests are permanently closed; only prospective future evaluation remains.

The secretary's framing is accurate. I will not reopen settled points.

The draft N2 one-sided Δ formulation is compatible with my position. I had proposed a two-sided |Δ|, but the one-sided test is acceptable.

I will accept the one-sided Δ formulation for the gate. I am ready to state my final position and compromise for each open dispute.

I will briefly confirm the near-settled items so they can settle. Then I will state my final positions and compromises for the three open disputes.

I will keep the response concrete and quantitative, avoiding hedging or boilerplate. I will not reopen settled points. I have verified that Kimi's claim about the first effective-n computation date is incorrect.

I will not veto the robustness print lines. My core argument for O1 is that the written §2 gate compares incommensurable scores: +2.19 pp versus a block MDE of 2.99, with effective n near 49 against 50.

The counter to my O1 position rests on the monthly gate’s 36.83 versus 32.23 and 29.24 versus 26.05 results, identical label overlap, and 800 versus 267 covariate readings. Fable, Opus, and Sol invoke the “spec governs code” principle as an outcome-independent rule. Kimi’s effective-sample argument was available when §2 was written. Sol also notes that λ=1 on 800 rows is weaker regularisation if loss is summed, which requires sealed normalisation.

I am reconsidering whether my O1 position is still best. The gate compares skills on different origin sets with different base rates, which is a bad decision rule. The only paired comparison—quarter-end thinning—fails by 0.02 pp, so it is noise. Fit and evaluation are not the same question.

A counterfactual test shows monthly and quarterly slope estimates differ by only about 0.12, with p-values near 14%. The ground rules forbid relaxing thresholds after the result is seen. The monthly gate passed the preregistered rule.

Overriding a preregistered gate because the test is misspecified is a governance choice, not a statistical finding of inferiority. Sol accepts this post-hoc governance choice without claiming demonstrated superiority. The skill difference of +2.19 pp against an MDE of 2.99 is not distinguishable.

The p-value gap is only 0.5 points, so both monthly and quarterly results sit inside their bands and are not distinguishable from the base rate. The slope shift from −1.29 to −1.41 is 9% steeper, but λ=1 on summed loss means this reflects a regularisation change rather than pure information gain. Sol’s point is decisive: switching frequency without sealing loss normalisation silently alters λ. If I concede monthly, the condition is sealed normalisation so that λ=1 means the same penalty per observation or episode, not per row count.

I have weighed two O1 compromises. One accepts monthly from 2027 with sealed normalisation and parallel quarterly publication. The other keeps quarterly, records the council overrode the preregistered gate, and treats monthly P as an unscored column. I still prefer quarterly because the operational gap is only 0.5 points inside the band, and switching now after seeing the slope steepen and P fall is a chosen decision.

The monthly gate is incommensurable. Overriding it is not a threshold relaxation; it is rejecting a misspecified comparison as if it were identified. Walk-forward skill does not improve in a paired sense. The quarter-end phase is worse at 26.03 versus 27.05. I am weighing whether the 0.5 point P shift justifies a veto. Both verdicts remain unchanged.

I will not veto the monthly compromise if it is sealed with parallel quarterly publication, no headline substitution, and a power clause on the actual configuration. Without those safeguards, silent λ rescaling would violate the settled point S1.

I will not veto monthly itself. I would only accept it if a paired skill comparison on common labels showed monthly fit beats quarterly by more than 1.96·SD_block, and the penalty is sealed per observation so the slope change is not just N-scaling. That evidence is absent. I would also reject the compromise if the sealed specification could not be pushed before the refit, or if +29.24 were allowed to replace the operational headline.

I rejected the content-triggered refit. The effect is tiny: mean |ΔP| is only 0.13 points, max 1.05, across just 53 of 588 months, yielding roughly six extra refits per 49 years. Claude’s compromise would allow one content-triggered refit per new onset, with later positives waiting for September; that still yields about six extra refits, not eighteen. Sol and DeepSeek favor a configuration-specific replay sealed and published. Fable requires counting trough-driven censoring flips, but the secretary reports none at lag ≤ 30. My objection is cost versus benefit and the small effect size.

The structural argument is that the lag depends on NBER timing. The projected benefit is only 0.37 points for the second and later positives of an episode. The first positive often matures in September anyway, so the compromise captures the largest effect at the scheduled refit and only accelerates later ones. Six deterministic refits per forty-nine years is a small cost for that gain.

I still reject the content-triggered refit. Extra refits between Septembers break the frozen-weight assumption and threaten ledger comparability unless each configuration is sealed and replayed. E5 power is already hopeless, so more refits do not help identification and would create a regime absent from historical replays.

The projected 0.37 point gain falls inside the October estimation-sensitivity band, so it is operationally invisible. The compromise is mechanical and preregistered rather than a threshold relaxation. It limits refits to one per new onset, so it is not a tuning lever. The September plus hash rule already delayed 85 origin months, some of which was the second positive waiting nine months. I have no strong econometric objection to ingesting a matured positive when it becomes eligible; my prior concern was churn and the tiny effect size. This compromise cuts churn by two-thirds.

I would not veto the one-per-onset compromise if it is restricted to the first new positive per onset, sealed with a configuration-specific replay published as a supplement, excludes negative-maturation triggers, and leaves weights frozen until the next September. I still prefer rejecting it outright. I can live with the compromise provided the public statement clarifies that historical ledger skill is not the operational regime’s skill. I would veto the full eighteen-refit version.

The eighteen-refit version is a process change whose only measured effect is below any band, chosen after seeing the result. That cost is not worth breaking the annual freeze. Evidence that would change a veto would need to show delayed ingestion costs more than 1.96·SD of ledger skill, or a delay exceeding nine months that moves P outside the published band; the maximum observed shift is only 1.05 points.

On O3 EBP, I am closing on a candidate text: the historical sealed test closes permanently once its onset pattern is seen, and EBP remains a context line.

I accept a future council’s prospective-only evaluation rule, provided it is sealed before any onset it would judge and pre-2027 data is excluded as evidence. The historical pattern is already seen across roughly five of eight onsets, so contamination is incurable. Baa remains closed under S6. N1 is confirmed: oracle-free fixed-λ leads with triple print.

I accept the power clause inline. The N2 draft is acceptable without 4.42: one-sided Δ above 1.96·SD_block triggers agenda, never evidence, never switch. Print 80% MDE ≈ 30 points via leave-one-block Δ and start-date Δ. I will use one-sided |Δ| for "F5 beats curve" and avoid calling 1.96·SD an MDE.

I will not veto auto-labelling a crossing as evidence or any switch; the draft already forbids both. For N3, I hold peak-only and accept a separate trough-lag parameter for the open-episode rule. Claude’s L_R equals 18 today. Kimi’s eligibility rule requires age at least L_R and resolved censoring status available at R.

The secretary’s fact is correct: historical max trough lag is 21, below the 30-month maturity threshold, so no censored-to-label-0 flip has occurred. Argon’s +4.54 point gain reflects scoring-censoring rather than eligible fit. I will not raise L_R to 21. I can live with either Claude’s formula or Kimi’s eligibility AND. Claude’s formula is cleaner because it yields a single auditable number that rises only if a future trough lag exceeds 30.

I now accept both the Claude floor and Kimi’s row-level rule as a compromise. The peak floor stays at 18, and the separate trough-lag parameter is written into the open-episode rule before the audit.

I would veto L_R = 21 as a permanent floor because the q+30 clock shows no censored-to-label-0 flip has ever occurred; the maximum observed trough lag is 21, below the 30-month threshold. Evidence that would change my mind: a historical origin that entered eligible_fit and later flipped censored→0 or 0→censored because a trough was announced after q+30. I will not raise the floor to 21.

N3 is near-settled rather than fully open, but I should state my position briefly to prevent Argon and Fable from assuming silence.

I will include a tight confirm block for N3.

For post-hoc acceptability, O1 is acceptable because the preregistered comparison is incommensurable across different sample sizes and base rates, and the operational P delta is only 0.5 points. Choosing monthly is also acceptable if framed as executing the written gate rather than as evidence that monthly is better, provided penalty normalisation is sealed so λ = 1 is not redefined.

O2 is acceptable as a pre-committed mechanical rule if the replay is sealed and skill improvement is not claimed. I am now drafting the tight veto list.

The tight veto list is now complete. Monthly fit is blocked without a sealed loss and penalty normalisation pushed before the refit, because that would redefine the settled λ = 1. The +29.24 headline and any claim of improvement over +27.05 are also blocked. The unrestricted eighteen-refit content trigger is vetoed, but one-per-onset with a sealed configuration-specific replay is not.

The draft is now structured into six sections: framing, N1–N3 confirmations, O1 compromise with its veto, O2 compromise with its veto, O3 compromise with its veto, and a folded-in “what would change my mind” note. The L_R = 21 floor is treated as a N3 veto because it would block consensus. The word budget is set at roughly six hundred words.

The monthly compromise is now defined: it applies only from 2027 onward, requires a sealed loss and penalty normalisation pushed before the refit so λ = 1 remains fixed per observation or episode, and quarterly walk-forward stays published in parallel for the model’s life. The operational headline remains the oracle-free figure for the configuration actually run, with no sentence claiming monthly is better. “Spec governs code” is adopted generally, but this override is minuted as executing a ratified non-inferiority gate rather than a skill finding.

The monthly override would reopen S1 without a sealed penalty normalisation. A paired comparison on a common label set and base rate, where monthly beats quarterly by more than 1.96·SD_block after per-observation normalisation, would change my mind.

O2: the unrestricted trigger is rejected. Mean |ΔP| is 0.13 points, maximum shift 1.05, and only 53 of 588 months show a gap. That does not justify eighteen extra refits or a break in the annual freeze.

The O2 compromise is now defined. Claude’s one-refit-per-onset rule applies: a single refit fires only for the first matured positive or relabel absent from the manifest, while later positives wait for September, and negative-maturation triggers are banned. This yields roughly six extra refits per forty-nine years. A configuration-specific replay must be sealed now and published as a supplement; the September-only figures are not described as the operational regime. The small historical ΔP is rejected as justification and as a success metric.
